1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Runs INSIDE the Apptainer container. Creates a Python venv on /scratch and
3	# installs rllm + verl + their RL deps from PyPI source — no cluster modules.
4	#
5	# Invoke from the project root, NOT from inside the container, like:
6	#   bash scripts/00_enter_container.sh scripts/01_build_env.sh
7	set -euo pipefail
8	
9	SCRATCH=${SCRATCH:-/scratch/$USER}
10	PROJECT_ROOT=${PROJECT_ROOT:-/project/def-hemmati-ac/$USER/SWE-Master}
11	VENV=${VENV:-$SCRATCH/swemaster/venv/rllm}
12	HF_HOME_DIR=${HF_HOME_DIR:-$SCRATCH/swemaster/cache/hf}
13	PIP_CACHE=${PIP_CACHE:-$SCRATCH/swemaster/cache/pip}
14	
15	mkdir -p "$VENV" "$HF_HOME_DIR" "$PIP_CACHE"
16	
17	# Use the container's python (3.11 inside pytorch:2.7.1-cu128 image)
18	PYTHON_BIN=${PYTHON_BIN:-$(command -v python3)}
19	echo "[build-env] python: $PYTHON_BIN -> $($PYTHON_BIN --version)"
20	echo "[build-env] venv:   $VENV"
21	echo "[build-env] HF:     $HF_HOME_DIR"
22	
23	if [[ ! -x "$VENV/bin/python" ]]; then
24	  "$PYTHON_BIN" -m venv "$VENV"
25	fi
26	
27	# shellcheck disable=SC1090
28	source "$VENV/bin/activate"
29	
30	export PIP_CACHE_DIR="$PIP_CACHE"
31	export PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK=1
32	
33	python -m pip install --upgrade pip wheel setuptools
34	
35	# Install torch first so dependent wheels resolve correctly. The container
36	# already ships torch 2.7.1+cu128 in /opt/conda — but a fresh venv won't see
37	# it. We use --extra-index-url to grab the matching CUDA 12.8 wheels.
38	pip install \
39	  --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128 \
40	  "torch==2.7.1" "torchvision" "torchaudio"
41	
42	# Install flash-attn FIRST, from a prebuilt wheel that matches our torch
43	# (2.7.1+cu128 cxx11abi=True python3.11). If pip ever tries to build from
44	# source it'll fail because rllm's transitive flash-attn>=2.8.0.post2 pull
45	# runs in an isolated build env that can't see torch.
46	FA_VER="2.8.3"
47	FA_WHL="flash_attn-${FA_VER}+cu12torch2.7cxx11abiTRUE-cp311-cp311-linux_x86_64.whl"
48	FA_URL="https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/releases/download/v${FA_VER}/${FA_WHL}"
49	pip install --no-build-isolation "$FA_URL" || {
50	  echo "[build-env] prebuilt flash-attn wheel not available, falling back to source build (slow)"
51	  MAX_JOBS=2 NVCC_THREADS=2 pip install --no-build-isolation "flash-attn==${FA_VER}"
52	}
53	
54	# --- (3) rllm: install editable with --no-deps. rllm pulls a huge dep tree
55	# (sglang, browsergym, selenium, gradio, firecrawl, ...) we don't need for
56	# the FrozenLake smoke test, and the unconstrained graph makes pip's
57	# resolver explode with "resolution-too-deep". Install the minimum set we
58	# actually need below.
59	pip install --no-deps -e "$PROJECT_ROOT/DeepSWE_RL/rllm"
60	
61	# Clone verl. README says v0.5 but no such tag exists upstream; release/v0.7.1
62	# is the latest stable. Note: the container has no `git`, so the clone must
63	# happen on the host (login node) before this script runs. We just verify
64	# here that the checkout is present.
65	VERL_DIR="$PROJECT_ROOT/DeepSWE_RL/rllm/verl"
66	if [[ ! -d "$VERL_DIR" ]]; then
67	  echo "[build-env] verl not found at $VERL_DIR — clone it on the host (which has git) first:" >&2
68	  echo "  git clone --depth 1 --branch release/v0.7.1 https://github.com/volcengine/verl.git $VERL_DIR" >&2
69	  exit 1
70	fi
71	pip install --no-deps -e "$VERL_DIR"
72	
73	# --- (4) Minimum-viable runtime dependencies for verl+rllm RL training ---
74	# Each line is intentional; do NOT collapse with `pip install A B C` if any
75	# package needs special index/url handling later.
76	pip install \
77	  "transformers>=4.45" \
78	  "accelerate>=0.34" \
79	  "datasets>=2.20" \
80	  "hydra-core>=1.3" \
81	  "omegaconf>=2.3" \
82	  "ray[default]>=2.30" \
83	  "tensorboard" \

91	  "numpy<2.0" \

96	  "psutil" \

99	  "dm-tree" \
100	  "gym>=0.26.2" \
101	  "fire" \
102	  "sentence-transformers" \
103	  "torchmetrics" \

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runs INSIDE the Apptainer container. Creates a Python venv on /scratch and
# installs rllm + verl + their RL deps from PyPI source — no cluster modules.
#
# Invoke from the project root, NOT from inside the container, like:
#   bash scripts/00_enter_container.sh scripts/01_build_env.sh
set -euo pipefail

SCRATCH=${SCRATCH:-/scratch/$USER}
PROJECT_ROOT=${PROJECT_ROOT:-/project/def-hemmati-ac/$USER/SWE-Master}
VENV=${VENV:-$SCRATCH/swemaster/venv/rllm}
HF_HOME_DIR=${HF_HOME_DIR:-$SCRATCH/swemaster/cache/hf}
PIP_CACHE=${PIP_CACHE:-$SCRATCH/swemaster/cache/pip}

mkdir -p "$VENV" "$HF_HOME_DIR" "$PIP_CACHE"

# Use the container's python (3.11 inside pytorch:2.7.1-cu128 image)
PYTHON_BIN=${PYTHON_BIN:-$(command -v python3)}
echo "[build-env] python: $PYTHON_BIN -> $($PYTHON_BIN --version)"
echo "[build-env] venv:   $VENV"
echo "[build-env] HF:     $HF_HOME_DIR"

if [[ ! -x "$VENV/bin/python" ]]; then
  "$PYTHON_BIN" -m venv "$VENV"
fi

# shellcheck disable=SC1090
source "$VENV/bin/activate"

export PIP_CACHE_DIR="$PIP_CACHE"
export PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK=1

python -m pip install --upgrade pip wheel setuptools

# Install torch first so dependent wheels resolve correctly. The container
# already ships torch 2.7.1+cu128 in /opt/conda — but a fresh venv won't see
# it. We use --extra-index-url to grab the matching CUDA 12.8 wheels.
pip install \
  --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128 \
  "torch==2.7.1" "torchvision" "torchaudio"

# Install flash-attn FIRST, from a prebuilt wheel that matches our torch
# (2.7.1+cu128 cxx11abi=True python3.11). If pip ever tries to build from
# source it'll fail because rllm's transitive flash-attn>=2.8.0.post2 pull
# runs in an isolated build env that can't see torch.
FA_VER="2.8.3"
FA_WHL="flash_attn-${FA_VER}+cu12torch2.7cxx11abiTRUE-cp311-cp311-linux_x86_64.whl"
FA_URL="https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/releases/download/v${FA_VER}/${FA_WHL}"
pip install --no-build-isolation "$FA_URL" || {
  echo "[build-env] prebuilt flash-attn wheel not available, falling back to source build (slow)"
  MAX_JOBS=2 NVCC_THREADS=2 pip install --no-build-isolation "flash-attn==${FA_VER}"
}

# --- (3) rllm: install editable with --no-deps. rllm pulls a huge dep tree
# (sglang, browsergym, selenium, gradio, firecrawl, ...) we don't need for
# the FrozenLake smoke test, and the unconstrained graph makes pip's
# resolver explode with "resolution-too-deep". Install the minimum set we
# actually need below.
pip install --no-deps -e "$PROJECT_ROOT/DeepSWE_RL/rllm"

# Clone verl. README says v0.5 but no such tag exists upstream; release/v0.7.1
# is the latest stable. Note: the container has no `git`, so the clone must
# happen on the host (login node) before this script runs. We just verify
# here that the checkout is present.
VERL_DIR="$PROJECT_ROOT/DeepSWE_RL/rllm/verl"
if [[ ! -d "$VERL_DIR" ]]; then
  echo "[build-env] verl not found at $VERL_DIR — clone it on the host (which has git) first:" >&2
  echo "  git clone --depth 1 --branch release/v0.7.1 https://github.com/volcengine/verl.git $VERL_DIR" >&2
  exit 1
fi
pip install --no-deps -e "$VERL_DIR"

# --- (4) Minimum-viable runtime dependencies for verl+rllm RL training ---
# Each line is intentional; do NOT collapse with `pip install A B C` if any
# package needs special index/url handling later.
pip install \
  "transformers>=4.45" \
  "accelerate>=0.34" \
  "datasets>=2.20" \
  "hydra-core>=1.3" \
  "omegaconf>=2.3" \
  "ray[default]>=2.30" \
  "tensorboard" \
  "tensorboardX" \
  "wandb" \
  "codetiming" \
  "polars" \
  "dill" \
  "pyarrow" \
  "pandas" \
  "numpy<2.0" \
  "scipy" \
  "tqdm" \
  "regex" \
  "pyyaml" \
  "psutil" \
  "peft" \
  "deepspeed" \
  "dm-tree" \
  "gym>=0.26.2" \
  "fire" \
  "sentence-transformers" \
  "torchmetrics" \
  "einops" \
  "msgpack" \
  "huggingface_hub"

# vllm last — it has very specific torch + cuda pins. Use a version that
# supports torch 2.7 + cu128.
pip install --no-build-isolation "vllm>=0.10,<0.11" || pip install "vllm"

# --- (5) sanity check ----------------------------------------------------
python - <<'PY'
import importlib, sys
for mod in ("torch", "flash_attn", "rllm", "verl", "vllm", "transformers",
            "ray", "hydra", "omegaconf", "tensorboard", "datasets"):
    try:
        m = importlib.import_module(mod)
        print(f"[ok] {mod:<16} {getattr(m,'__version__','?')}  {getattr(m,'__file__','?')[:80]}")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"[MISS] {mod}: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
PY
echo "[build-env] DONE"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runs INSIDE the Apptainer container. Creates a Python venv on /scratch and
# installs rllm + verl + their RL deps from PyPI source — no cluster modules.
#
# Invoke from the project root, NOT from inside the container, like:
#   bash scripts/00_enter_container.sh scripts/01_build_env.sh
set -euo pipefail

SCRATCH=${SCRATCH:-/scratch/$USER}
PROJECT_ROOT=${PROJECT_ROOT:-/project/def-hemmati-ac/$USER/SWE-Master}
VENV=${VENV:-$SCRATCH/swemaster/venv/rllm}
HF_HOME_DIR=${HF_HOME_DIR:-$SCRATCH/swemaster/cache/hf}
PIP_CACHE=${PIP_CACHE:-$SCRATCH/swemaster/cache/pip}

mkdir -p "$VENV" "$HF_HOME_DIR" "$PIP_CACHE"

# Use the container's python (3.11 inside pytorch:2.7.1-cu128 image)
PYTHON_BIN=${PYTHON_BIN:-$(command -v python3)}
echo "[build-env] python: $PYTHON_BIN -> $($PYTHON_BIN --version)"
echo "[build-env] venv:   $VENV"
echo "[build-env] HF:     $HF_HOME_DIR"

if [[ ! -x "$VENV/bin/python" ]]; then
  "$PYTHON_BIN" -m venv "$VENV"
fi

# shellcheck disable=SC1090
source "$VENV/bin/activate"

export PIP_CACHE_DIR="$PIP_CACHE"
export PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK=1

python -m pip install --upgrade pip wheel setuptools

# (1) Install vllm FIRST so it gets to pick the torch version it needs.
# vllm 0.10.x pulls torch 2.8.0+cu128 as a hard requirement. Installing it
# AFTER torch 2.7 would have the bad surprise of silently upgrading torch
# and breaking any C-extensions already built against 2.7.
pip install "vllm>=0.10,<0.11"

# (2) flash-attn from prebuilt wheel matched to torch 2.8 + cu12 + cp311 +
# cxx11abi=True. PyPI's flash-attn never has a wheel; only github releases do.
FA_VER="2.8.3"
FA_WHL="flash_attn-${FA_VER}+cu12torch2.8cxx11abiTRUE-cp311-cp311-linux_x86_64.whl"
FA_URL="https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/releases/download/v${FA_VER}/${FA_WHL}"
pip install --no-build-isolation "$FA_URL"

# (3) Editable installs of this repo's rllm and verl (already cloned on host).
pip install --no-deps -e "$PROJECT_ROOT/DeepSWE_RL/rllm"

VERL_DIR="$PROJECT_ROOT/DeepSWE_RL/rllm/verl"
if [[ ! -d "$VERL_DIR" ]]; then
  echo "[build-env] verl not found at $VERL_DIR — clone it on the host first:" >&2
  echo "  git clone --depth 1 --branch release/v0.7.1 https://github.com/volcengine/verl.git $VERL_DIR" >&2
  exit 1
fi
pip install --no-deps -e "$VERL_DIR"

# (4) Runtime deps. Pin numpy<2.0 LAST so it sticks (vllm pulls 2.x).
pip install \
  "transformers>=4.45" \
  "accelerate>=0.34" \
  "datasets>=2.20" \
  "hydra-core>=1.3" \
  "omegaconf>=2.3" \
  "ray[default]>=2.30" \
  "tensorboard" \
  "tensorboardX" \
  "wandb" \
  "codetiming" \
  "polars" \
  "dill" \
  "pyarrow" \
  "pandas" \
  "scipy" \
  "tqdm" \
  "regex" \
  "pyyaml" \
  "psutil" \
  "peft" \
  "deepspeed" \
  "dm-tree" \
  "gym>=0.26.2" \
  "fire" \
  "sentence-transformers" \
  "torchmetrics" \
  "einops" \
  "msgpack" \
  "huggingface_hub" \
  "tensordict>=0.8,<=0.10" \
  "torchdata" \
  "pybind11" \
  "pylatexenc"

# Re-pin numpy<2.0 last (vllm + several deps default to numpy 2.x which
# breaks verl + flash-attn).
pip install "numpy<2.0"

# --- (5) sanity check ----------------------------------------------------
python - <<'PY'
import importlib, sys
for mod in ("torch", "flash_attn", "rllm", "verl", "vllm", "transformers",
            "ray", "hydra", "omegaconf", "tensorboard", "datasets"):

    except Exception as e:
        print(f"[MISS] {mod}: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runs INSIDE the Apptainer container. Creates a Python venv on /scratch and
# installs rllm + verl + their RL deps from PyPI source — no cluster modules.
#
# Invoke from the project root, NOT from inside the container, like:
#   bash scripts/00_enter_container.sh scripts/01_build_env.sh
set -euo pipefail

SCRATCH=${SCRATCH:-/scratch/$USER}
PROJECT_ROOT=${PROJECT_ROOT:-/project/def-hemmati-ac/$USER/SWE-Master}
VENV=${VENV:-$SCRATCH/swemaster/venv/rllm}
HF_HOME_DIR=${HF_HOME_DIR:-$SCRATCH/swemaster/cache/hf}
PIP_CACHE=${PIP_CACHE:-$SCRATCH/swemaster/cache/pip}

mkdir -p "$VENV" "$HF_HOME_DIR" "$PIP_CACHE"

# Use the container's python (3.11 inside pytorch:2.7.1-cu128 image)
PYTHON_BIN=${PYTHON_BIN:-$(command -v python3)}
echo "[build-env] python: $PYTHON_BIN -> $($PYTHON_BIN --version)"
echo "[build-env] venv:   $VENV"
echo "[build-env] HF:     $HF_HOME_DIR"

if [[ ! -x "$VENV/bin/python" ]]; then
  "$PYTHON_BIN" -m venv "$VENV"
fi

# shellcheck disable=SC1090
source "$VENV/bin/activate"

export PIP_CACHE_DIR="$PIP_CACHE"
export PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK=1

python -m pip install --upgrade pip wheel setuptools

# (1) Install vllm FIRST so it gets to pick the torch version it needs.
# vllm 0.10.x pulls torch 2.8.0+cu128 as a hard requirement. Installing it
# AFTER torch 2.7 would have the bad surprise of silently upgrading torch
# and breaking any C-extensions already built against 2.7.
pip install "vllm>=0.10,<0.11"

# (2) flash-attn from prebuilt wheel matched to torch 2.8 + cu12 + cp311 +
# cxx11abi=True. PyPI's flash-attn never has a wheel; only github releases do.
# --force-reinstall is required because pip strips the local-version tag
# (+cu12torch2.8cxx11abiTRUE) when comparing installed vs requested, so a
# stale wheel built against a different torch would be silently kept.
FA_VER="2.8.3"
FA_WHL="flash_attn-${FA_VER}+cu12torch2.8cxx11abiTRUE-cp311-cp311-linux_x86_64.whl"
FA_URL="https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/releases/download/v${FA_VER}/${FA_WHL}"
pip install --no-build-isolation --force-reinstall --no-deps "$FA_URL"

# (3) Editable installs of this repo's rllm and verl (already cloned on host).
pip install --no-deps -e "$PROJECT_ROOT/DeepSWE_RL/rllm"

VERL_DIR="$PROJECT_ROOT/DeepSWE_RL/rllm/verl"
if [[ ! -d "$VERL_DIR" ]]; then
  echo "[build-env] verl not found at $VERL_DIR — clone it on the host first:" >&2
  echo "  git clone --depth 1 --branch release/v0.7.1 https://github.com/volcengine/verl.git $VERL_DIR" >&2
  exit 1
fi
pip install --no-deps -e "$VERL_DIR"

# (4) Runtime deps. Pin numpy<2.0 LAST so it sticks (vllm pulls 2.x).
pip install \
  "transformers>=4.45" \
  "accelerate>=0.34" \
  "datasets>=2.20" \
  "hydra-core>=1.3" \
  "omegaconf>=2.3" \
  "ray[default]>=2.30" \
  "tensorboard" \
  "tensorboardX" \
  "wandb" \
  "codetiming" \
  "polars" \
  "dill" \
  "pyarrow" \
  "pandas" \
  "scipy" \
  "tqdm" \
  "regex" \
  "pyyaml" \
  "psutil" \
  "peft" \
  "deepspeed" \
  "dm-tree" \
  "gym>=0.26.2" \
  "fire" \
  "sentence-transformers" \
  "torchmetrics" \
  "einops" \
  "msgpack" \
  "huggingface_hub" \
  "tensordict>=0.8,<=0.10" \
  "torchdata" \
  "pybind11" \
  "pylatexenc"

# Re-pin numpy<2.0 last (vllm + several deps default to numpy 2.x which
# breaks verl + flash-attn).
pip install "numpy<2.0"

# --- (5) sanity check ----------------------------------------------------
python - <<'PY'
import importlib, sys
for mod in ("torch", "flash_attn", "rllm", "verl", "vllm", "transformers",
            "ray", "hydra", "omegaconf", "tensorboard", "datasets"):
    try:
        m = importlib.import_module(mod)
        print(f"[ok] {mod:<16} {getattr(m,'__version__','?')}  {getattr(m,'__file__','?')[:80]}")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"[MISS] {mod}: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
PY
echo "[build-env] DONE"

|---|---|---|
| Apptainer sandbox (PyTorch 2.8 + CUDA 12.8) | ✅ | `/scratch/moham98/swemaster/sif/pytorch_27_cu128/` (16 GB) |

| Smoke training launch | ⏳ | yours to trigger |

## Smoke run

The training script doesn't need any further patching. From a GPU-bearing shell (whatever interactive/allocation method you prefer), run:

```bash
cd /project/def-hemmati-ac/moham98/SWE-Master
bash scripts/00_enter_container.sh bash scripts/04_train_frozenlake.sh
```

The script defaults to `N_GPUS=4`, `total_training_steps=5`, `trainer.logger=['console','tensorboard']`. You can override e.g. `N_GPUS=1 bash …`. Per-step scalars will print on stdout (verl's `Tracking`) and write to `/scratch/$USER/swemaster/runs/rllm-smoke/<experiment>/` for tensorboard.

content.content:
1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Runs INSIDE the Apptainer container. Creates a Python venv on /scratch and
3	# installs rllm + verl + their RL deps from PyPI source — no cluster modules.
4	#
5	# Invoke from the project root, NOT from inside the container, like:
6	#   bash scripts/00_enter_container.sh scripts/01_build_env.sh
7	set -euo pipefail
8	
9	SCRATCH=${SCRATCH:-/scratch/$USER}
10	PROJECT_ROOT=${PROJECT_ROOT:-/project/def-hemmati-ac/$USER/SWE-Master}
11	VENV=${VENV:-$SCRATCH/swemaster/venv/rllm}
12	HF_HOME_DIR=${HF_HOME_DIR:-$SCRATCH/swemaster/cache/hf}
13	PIP_CACHE=${PIP_CACHE:-$SCRATCH/swemaster/cache/pip}
14	
15	mkdir -p "$VENV" "$HF_HOME_DIR" "$PIP_CACHE"
16	
17	# Use the container's python (3.11 inside pytorch:2.7.1-cu128 image)
18	PYTHON_BIN=${PYTHON_BIN:-$(command -v python3)}
19	echo "[build-env] python: $PYTHON_BIN -> $($PYTHON_BIN --version)"
20	echo "[build-env] venv:   $VENV"
21	echo "[build-env] HF:     $HF_HOME_DIR"
22	
23	if [[ ! -x "$VENV/bin/python" ]]; then
24	  "$PYTHON_BIN" -m venv "$VENV"
25	fi
26	
27	# shellcheck disable=SC1090
28	source "$VENV/bin/activate"
29	
30	export PIP_CACHE_DIR="$PIP_CACHE"
31	export PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK=1
32	
33	python -m pip install --upgrade pip wheel setuptools
34	
35	# (1) Install vllm FIRST so it gets to pick the torch version it needs.
36	# vllm 0.10.x pulls torch 2.8.0+cu128 as a hard requirement. Installing it
37	# AFTER torch 2.7 would have the bad surprise of silently upgrading torch
38	# and breaking any C-extensions already built against 2.7.
39	pip install "vllm>=0.10,<0.11"
40	
41	# (2) flash-attn from prebuilt wheel matched to torch 2.8 + cu12 + cp311 +
42	# cxx11abi=True. PyPI's flash-attn never has a wheel; only github releases do.
43	# --force-reinstall is required because pip strips the local-version tag
44	# (+cu12torch2.8cxx11abiTRUE) when comparing installed vs requested, so a
45	# stale wheel built against a different torch would be silently kept.
46	FA_VER="2.8.3"
47	FA_WHL="flash_attn-${FA_VER}+cu12torch2.8cxx11abiTRUE-cp311-cp311-linux_x86_64.whl"
48	FA_URL="https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/releases/download/v${FA_VER}/${FA_WHL}"
49	pip install --no-build-isolation --force-reinstall --no-deps "$FA_URL"
50	
51	# (3) Editable installs of this repo's rllm and verl (already cloned on host).
52	pip install --no-deps -e "$PROJECT_ROOT/DeepSWE_RL/rllm"
53	
54	VERL_DIR="$PROJECT_ROOT/DeepSWE_RL/rllm/verl"
55	if [[ ! -d "$VERL_DIR" ]]; then
56	  echo "[build-env] verl not found at $VERL_DIR — clone it on the host first:" >&2
57	  echo "  git clone --depth 1 --branch release/v0.7.1 https://github.com/volcengine/verl.git $VERL_DIR" >&2
58	  exit 1
59	fi
60	pip install --no-deps -e "$VERL_DIR"
61	
62	# (4) Runtime deps. Pin numpy<2.0 LAST so it sticks (vllm pulls 2.x).
63	pip install \
64	  "transformers>=4.45" \
65	  "accelerate>=0.34" \
66	  "datasets>=2.20" \
67	  "hydra-core>=1.3" \
68	  "omegaconf>=2.3" \
69	  "ray[default]>=2.30" \
70	  "tensorboard" \
71	  "tensorboardX" \
72	  "wandb" \
73	  "codetiming" \
74	  "polars" \
75	  "dill" \
76	  "pyarrow" \
77	  "pandas" \
78	  "scipy" \
79	  "tqdm" \
80	  "regex" \
81	  "pyyaml" \
82	  "psutil" \
83	  "peft" \
84	  "deepspeed" \
85	  "dm-tree" \
86	  "gym>=0.26.2" \

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runs INSIDE the Apptainer container. Creates a Python venv on /scratch and
# installs rllm + verl + their RL deps from PyPI source — no cluster modules.
#
# Invoke from the project root, NOT from inside the container, like:
#   bash scripts/00_enter_container.sh scripts/01_build_env.sh
set -euo pipefail

SCRATCH=${SCRATCH:-/scratch/$USER}
PROJECT_ROOT=${PROJECT_ROOT:-/project/def-hemmati-ac/$USER/SWE-Master}
VENV=${VENV:-$SCRATCH/swemaster/venv/rllm}
HF_HOME_DIR=${HF_HOME_DIR:-$SCRATCH/swemaster/cache/hf}
PIP_CACHE=${PIP_CACHE:-$SCRATCH/swemaster/cache/pip}

mkdir -p "$VENV" "$HF_HOME_DIR" "$PIP_CACHE"

# Use the container's python (3.11 inside pytorch:2.7.1-cu128 image)
PYTHON_BIN=${PYTHON_BIN:-$(command -v python3)}
echo "[build-env] python: $PYTHON_BIN -> $($PYTHON_BIN --version)"
echo "[build-env] venv:   $VENV"
echo "[build-env] HF:     $HF_HOME_DIR"

if [[ ! -x "$VENV/bin/python" ]]; then
  "$PYTHON_BIN" -m venv "$VENV"
fi

# shellcheck disable=SC1090
source "$VENV/bin/activate"

export PIP_CACHE_DIR="$PIP_CACHE"
export PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK=1

python -m pip install --upgrade pip wheel setuptools

# (1) Install vllm FIRST so it gets to pick the torch version it needs.
# vllm 0.10.x pulls torch 2.8.0+cu128 as a hard requirement. Installing it
# AFTER torch 2.7 would have the bad surprise of silently upgrading torch
# and breaking any C-extensions already built against 2.7.
pip install "vllm>=0.10,<0.11"

# (2) flash-attn from prebuilt wheel matched to torch 2.8 + cu12 + cp311 +
# cxx11abi=True. PyPI's flash-attn never has a wheel; only github releases do.
# --force-reinstall is required because pip strips the local-version tag
# (+cu12torch2.8cxx11abiTRUE) when comparing installed vs requested, so a
# stale wheel built against a different torch would be silently kept.
FA_VER="2.8.3"
FA_WHL="flash_attn-${FA_VER}+cu12torch2.8cxx11abiTRUE-cp311-cp311-linux_x86_64.whl"
FA_URL="https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/releases/download/v${FA_VER}/${FA_WHL}"
pip install --no-build-isolation --force-reinstall --no-deps "$FA_URL"

# (3) Editable installs of this repo's rllm and verl (already cloned on host).
pip install --no-deps -e "$PROJECT_ROOT/DeepSWE_RL/rllm"

VERL_DIR="$PROJECT_ROOT/DeepSWE_RL/rllm/verl"
if [[ ! -d "$VERL_DIR" ]]; then
  echo "[build-env] verl not found at $VERL_DIR — clone it on the host first:" >&2
  echo "  git clone --depth 1 --branch release/v0.7.1 https://github.com/volcengine/verl.git $VERL_DIR" >&2
  exit 1
fi
pip install --no-deps -e "$VERL_DIR"

# (4) Runtime deps. Pin numpy<2.0 LAST so it sticks (vllm pulls 2.x).
pip install \
  "transformers>=4.45" \
  "accelerate>=0.34" \
  "datasets>=2.20" \
  "hydra-core>=1.3" \
  "omegaconf>=2.3" \
  "ray[default]>=2.30" \
  "tensorboard" \
  "tensorboardX" \
  "wandb" \
  "codetiming" \
  "polars" \
  "dill" \
  "pyarrow" \
  "pandas" \
  "scipy" \
  "tqdm" \
  "regex" \
  "pyyaml" \
  "psutil" \
  "peft" \
  "deepspeed" \
  "dm-tree" \
  "gym>=0.26.2" \
  "gymnasium[toy-text]>=1.0" \
  "fire" \
  "sentence-transformers" \
  "torchmetrics" \
  "einops" \
  "msgpack" \
  "huggingface_hub" \
  "tensordict>=0.8,<=0.10" \
  "torchdata" \
  "pybind11" \
  "pylatexenc"

# Re-pin numpy<2.0 last (vllm + several deps default to numpy 2.x which
# breaks verl + flash-attn).
pip install "numpy<2.0"

# --- (5) sanity check ----------------------------------------------------
python - <<'PY'
import importlib, sys
for mod in ("torch", "flash_attn", "rllm", "verl", "vllm", "transformers",
            "ray", "hydra", "omegaconf", "tensorboard", "datasets"):
    try:
        m = importlib.import_module(mod)
        print(f"[ok] {mod:<16} {getattr(m,'__version__','?')}  {getattr(m,'__file__','?')[:80]}")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"[MISS] {mod}: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
PY
echo "[build-env] DONE"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Smoke-test RL training: GRPO on FrozenLake with Qwen3-4B on a single node
# (4x H100 80GB on Trillium). Logs to console + tensorboard.
# Run inside the container — usually invoked by 04_train_frozenlake.sbatch.
set -euo pipefail

source "${VENV_BIN:-/scratch/$USER/swemaster/venv/rllm/bin}/activate"
cd "${PROJECT_ROOT:-/project/def-hemmati-ac/$USER/SWE-Master}/DeepSWE_RL/rllm"

export VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND=FLASH_ATTN
export PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF="expandable_segments:False"
export VLLM_USE_V1=1
export VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1
export VLLM_ENGINE_ITERATION_TIMEOUT_S=100000000000
export HYDRA_FULL_ERROR=1
export RAY_DEDUP_LOGS=0
export WANDB_MODE=offline

# How many GPUs to use for training. Trillium nodes are 4x H100.
N_GPUS=${N_GPUS:-4}

# Run identifier for tensorboard + checkpoint dirs.
TS=$(date +"%Y-%m-%d_%H-%M-%S")
PROJECT_NAME=${PROJECT_NAME:-"rllm-smoke"}
EXPERIMENT_NAME=${EXPERIMENT_NAME:-"frozenlake-qwen3-4b-${TS}"}
RUN_ROOT=${RUN_ROOT:-/scratch/$USER/swemaster/runs}
LOCAL_DIR="${RUN_ROOT}/${PROJECT_NAME}/${EXPERIMENT_NAME}"
mkdir -p "${LOCAL_DIR}"
echo "[train] LOCAL_DIR=${LOCAL_DIR}"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runs INSIDE the Apptainer container. Creates a Python venv on /scratch and
# installs rllm + verl + their RL deps from PyPI source — no cluster modules.
#
# Invoke from the project root, NOT from inside the container, like:
#   bash scripts/00_enter_container.sh scripts/01_build_env.sh
set -euo pipefail

SCRATCH=${SCRATCH:-/scratch/$USER}
PROJECT_ROOT=${PROJECT_ROOT:-/project/def-hemmati-ac/$USER/SWE-Master}
VENV=${VENV:-$SCRATCH/swemaster/venv/rllm}
HF_HOME_DIR=${HF_HOME_DIR:-$SCRATCH/swemaster/cache/hf}
PIP_CACHE=${PIP_CACHE:-$SCRATCH/swemaster/cache/pip}

mkdir -p "$VENV" "$HF_HOME_DIR" "$PIP_CACHE"

# Use the container's python (3.11 inside pytorch:2.7.1-cu128 image)
PYTHON_BIN=${PYTHON_BIN:-$(command -v python3)}
echo "[build-env] python: $PYTHON_BIN -> $($PYTHON_BIN --version)"
echo "[build-env] venv:   $VENV"
echo "[build-env] HF:     $HF_HOME_DIR"

if [[ ! -x "$VENV/bin/python" ]]; then
  "$PYTHON_BIN" -m venv "$VENV"
fi

# shellcheck disable=SC1090
source "$VENV/bin/activate"

export PIP_CACHE_DIR="$PIP_CACHE"
export PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK=1

python -m pip install --upgrade pip wheel setuptools

# (1) Install vllm FIRST so it gets to pick the torch version it needs.
# vllm 0.10.x pulls torch 2.8.0+cu128 as a hard requirement. Installing it
# AFTER torch 2.7 would have the bad surprise of silently upgrading torch
# and breaking any C-extensions already built against 2.7.
pip install "vllm>=0.10,<0.11"

# (2) flash-attn from prebuilt wheel matched to torch 2.8 + cu12 + cp311 +
# cxx11abi=True. PyPI's flash-attn never has a wheel; only github releases do.
# --force-reinstall is required because pip strips the local-version tag
# (+cu12torch2.8cxx11abiTRUE) when comparing installed vs requested, so a
# stale wheel built against a different torch would be silently kept.
FA_VER="2.8.3"
FA_WHL="flash_attn-${FA_VER}+cu12torch2.8cxx11abiTRUE-cp311-cp311-linux_x86_64.whl"
FA_URL="https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/releases/download/v${FA_VER}/${FA_WHL}"
pip install --no-build-isolation --force-reinstall --no-deps "$FA_URL"

# (3) Editable installs of this repo's rllm and verl (already cloned on host).
pip install --no-deps -e "$PROJECT_ROOT/DeepSWE_RL/rllm"

VERL_DIR="$PROJECT_ROOT/DeepSWE_RL/rllm/verl"
if [[ ! -d "$VERL_DIR" ]]; then
  echo "[build-env] verl not found at $VERL_DIR — clone it on the host first:" >&2
  echo "  git clone --depth 1 --branch release/v0.7.1 https://github.com/volcengine/verl.git $VERL_DIR" >&2
  exit 1
fi
pip install --no-deps -e "$VERL_DIR"

# (4) Runtime deps. Pin numpy<2.0 LAST so it sticks (vllm pulls 2.x).
pip install \
  "transformers>=4.45" \
  "accelerate>=0.34" \
  "datasets>=2.20" \
  "hydra-core>=1.3" \
  "omegaconf>=2.3" \
  "ray[default]>=2.30" \
  "tensorboard" \
  "tensorboardX" \
  "wandb" \
  "codetiming" \
  "polars" \
  "dill" \
  "pyarrow" \
  "pandas" \
  "scipy" \
  "tqdm" \
  "regex" \
  "pyyaml" \
  "psutil" \
  "peft" \
  "deepspeed" \
  "dm-tree" \
  "gym>=0.26.2" \
  "gymnasium[toy-text]>=1.0" \
  "fire" \
  "sentence-transformers" \
  "torchmetrics" \
  "einops" \
  "msgpack" \
  "huggingface_hub" \
  "tensordict>=0.8,<=0.10" \
  "torchdata" \
  "pybind11" \
  "pylatexenc"

# Re-pin numpy<2.0 last (vllm + several deps default to numpy 2.x which
# breaks verl + flash-attn).
pip install "numpy<2.0"

# --- (5) sanity check ----------------------------------------------------
python - <<'PY'
import importlib, sys
for mod in ("torch", "flash_attn", "rllm", "verl", "vllm", "transformers",
            "ray", "hydra", "omegaconf", "tensorboard", "datasets"):
    try:
        m = importlib.import_module(mod)
        print(f"[ok] {mod:<16} {getattr(m,'__version__','?')}  {getattr(m,'__file__','?')[:80]}")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"[MISS] {mod}: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
PY
echo "[build-env] DONE"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Smoke-test RL training: GRPO on FrozenLake with Qwen3-4B on a single node
# (4x H100 80GB on Trillium). Logs to console + tensorboard.
# Run inside the container — usually invoked by 04_train_frozenlake.sbatch.
set -euo pipefail

source "${VENV_BIN:-/scratch/$USER/swemaster/venv/rllm/bin}/activate"
cd "${PROJECT_ROOT:-/project/def-hemmati-ac/$USER/SWE-Master}/DeepSWE_RL/rllm"

export VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND=FLASH_ATTN
export PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF="expandable_segments:False"
export VLLM_USE_V1=1
export VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1
export VLLM_ENGINE_ITERATION_TIMEOUT_S=100000000000
export HYDRA_FULL_ERROR=1
export RAY_DEDUP_LOGS=0
export WANDB_MODE=offline

# How many GPUs to use for training. Trillium nodes are 4x H100.
N_GPUS=${N_GPUS:-4}

# Run identifier for tensorboard + checkpoint dirs.
TS=$(date +"%Y-%m-%d_%H-%M-%S")
PROJECT_NAME=${PROJECT_NAME:-"rllm-smoke"}
EXPERIMENT_NAME=${EXPERIMENT_NAME:-"frozenlake-qwen3-4b-${TS}"}
RUN_ROOT=${RUN_ROOT:-/scratch/$USER/swemaster/runs}
LOCAL_DIR="${RUN_ROOT}/${PROJECT_NAME}/${EXPERIMENT_NAME}"
mkdir -p "${LOCAL_DIR}"
echo "[train] LOCAL_DIR=${LOCAL_DIR}"

# Model path: prefer locally-cached snapshot to avoid hitting HF inside Ray
# workers. Fall back to repo id (will redownload via HF_HOME cache).
MODEL_ID=${MODEL_ID:-Qwen/Qwen3-4B}
HF_HUB="${HUGGINGFACE_HUB_CACHE:-${HF_HOME_DIR:-/scratch/$USER/swemaster/cache/hf}/hub}"
MODEL_PATH=$(python - <<PY
import os, glob
hub = os.environ.get("HF_HUB")
repo = os.environ.get("MODEL_ID","Qwen/Qwen3-4B").replace("/","--")
snapshots = glob.glob(os.path.join(hub, f"models--{repo}", "snapshots", "*"))
print(snapshots[0] if snapshots else os.environ["MODEL_ID"])
PY
)
echo "[train] MODEL_PATH=${MODEL_PATH}"

python -m examples.frozenlake.train_frozenlake_agent \
    algorithm.adv_estimator=grpo \
    data.train_batch_size=16 \

    actor_rollout_ref.model.use_remove_padding=True \
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.loss_agg_mode=seq-mean-token-sum \
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size=8 \
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_dynamic_bsz=True \
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_max_token_len_per_gpu=16000 \
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_kl_loss=False \
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.clip_ratio_high=0.28 \
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_coef=0.001 \
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_type=low_var_kl \
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.ulysses_sequence_parallel_size=1 \
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.grad_norm_threshold=10 \
    actor_rollout_ref.model.enable_gradient_checkpointing=True \
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.param_offload=True \
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.optimizer_offload=True \
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.tensor_model_parallel_size=1 \
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.name=vllm \
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.mode="async" \
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.chat_scheduler=verl.schedulers.completions_scheduler.CompletionsScheduler \
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.enforce_eager=False \
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.temperature=0.7 \
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.gpu_memory_utilization=0.7 \

    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.val_kwargs.top_p=0.8 \

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Smoke-test RL training: GRPO on FrozenLake with Qwen3-4B on a single node
# (4x H100 80GB on Trillium). Logs to console + tensorboard.
# Run inside the container — usually invoked by 04_train_frozenlake.sbatch.
set -euo pipefail

source "${VENV_BIN:-/scratch/$USER/swemaster/venv/rllm/bin}/activate"
cd "${PROJECT_ROOT:-/project/def-hemmati-ac/$USER/SWE-Master}/DeepSWE_RL/rllm"

export VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND=FLASH_ATTN
export PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF="expandable_segments:False"
export VLLM_USE_V1=1
export VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1
export VLLM_ENGINE_ITERATION_TIMEOUT_S=100000000000
export HYDRA_FULL_ERROR=1
export RAY_DEDUP_LOGS=0
export WANDB_MODE=offline

# How many GPUs to use for training. Trillium nodes are 4x H100.
N_GPUS=${N_GPUS:-4}

# Run identifier for tensorboard + checkpoint dirs.
TS=$(date +"%Y-%m-%d_%H-%M-%S")
PROJECT_NAME=${PROJECT_NAME:-"rllm-smoke"}
EXPERIMENT_NAME=${EXPERIMENT_NAME:-"frozenlake-qwen3-4b-${TS}"}

LOCAL_DIR="${RUN_ROOT}/${PROJECT_NAME}/${EXPERIMENT_NAME}"
mkdir -p "${LOCAL_DIR}"

# Model path: prefer locally-cached snapshot to avoid hitting HF inside Ray
# workers. Fall back to repo id (will redownload via HF_HOME cache).

import os, glob

repo = os.environ.get("MODEL_ID","Qwen/Qwen3-4B").replace("/","--")
snapshots = glob.glob(os.path.join(hub, f"models--{repo}", "snapshots", "*"))

PY
)

from typing import Any

import ray

from rllm.data import Dataset
from rllm.trainer.verl.train_agent_ppo import train_agent


class AgentTrainer:
    """
    A wrapper class that allows users to easily train custom agents with custom environments
    without having to directly interact with the underlying training infrastructure.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        agent_class: type,
        env_class: type,
        agent_args: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
        env_args: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
        config: dict[str, Any] | list[str] | None = None,
        train_dataset: Dataset | None = None,
        val_dataset: Dataset | None = None,
    ):
        """
        Initialize the AgentTrainer.

        Args:
            agent_class: The custom agent class to use for training
            env_class: The custom environment class to use for training
            config: Configuration overrides to apply to the default config
                   Can be a dictionary with dot notation keys (e.g., {"data.train_batch_size": 8})
                   or a list of strings in the format "key=value" (e.g., ["data.train_batch_size=8"])
            train_dataset: Optional train dataset to use
            val_dataset: Optional validation dataset to use
            agent_args: Optional arguments to pass to the agent class
            env_args: Optional arguments to pass to the environment class
        """
        self.agent_class = agent_class
        self.env_class = env_class
        self.agent_args = agent_args or {}
        self.env_args = env_args or {}

        self.config = config

        if train_dataset is not None and self.config is not None and hasattr(self.config, "data"):
            self.config.data.train_files = train_dataset.get_verl_data_path()
        if val_dataset is not None and self.config is not None and hasattr(self.config, "data"):
            self.config.data.val_files = val_dataset.get_verl_data_path()

    def train(self):
        if not ray.is_initialized():
            ray.init(runtime_env={
                "env_vars": {"TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM": "true", "NCCL_DEBUG": "WARN"},
                "pip": ["sentence_transformers"],})

        ray.get(train_agent.remote(self.config, self.agent_class, self.env_class, self.agent_args, self.env_args))

content.text:
This is a hard ceiling we can't engineer around from inside the container:

- **Hard limit on this login node**: `ulimit -u 1024` (soft = hard, can't raise without root).
- **Ray's `raylet`** is a separate C++ executable that creates a `boost::asio::thread_pool` sized to `hardware_concurrency()` (192 on this node). It tries to spawn ~192 internal threads at boot. Add the GCS server, log monitor, plasma store, dashboard_agent, multiple FSDP worker processes, vLLM worker processes — and you blow past 1024 instantly. The first thread that fails with `EAGAIN` aborts `raylet` via SIGABRT.
- **`taskset` doesn't help**: `boost::asio` reads `sysconf(_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN)`, not CPU affinity. We tested: even with `taskset -c 0-31`, `os.cpu_count()` still returns 192.
- **No `RAY_*` env var** exposes the raylet's internal `boost::asio` pool size.

So GRPO RL training using verl + ray + vLLM cannot run on this login node, period. Two paths forward:

content.text:
Here's the situation in plain terms:

## What's blocking us

**The setting**: We're on `trig-login01`, a *login node* — a small entry point you SSH into. It has 4 H100 GPUs sitting idle (we tested: 0% util, ready to use). The CPU side of the box is huge (192 cores). Login nodes are deliberately throttled so a single user can't accidentally hog them and starve everyone else.

**The throttle that's killing us**: `ulimit -u 1024`. This means *your user account can have at most 1024 processes-or-threads in existence at any moment, across all your SSH sessions combined*. We confirmed:
- Soft limit: 1024
- Hard limit: 1024 (can't raise without `root`)
- Already used by your existing shells/agents: ~30

So we have a budget of roughly **990 new threads/processes** for everything we launch.

## Why that budget can't fit our training stack

The RL trainer in this repo (rllm + verl + GRPO) is built on top of three big concurrency systems, each of which spawns many internal threads:

| Component | Threads it spawns | Configurable? |
|---|---|---|
| **Ray** `raylet` (C++ daemon) | `boost::asio::thread_pool` sized to `hardware_concurrency()` = **192** on this node | ❌ No public env var |
| **Ray** GCS server, dashboard, log monitor, plasma store, agent | ~50–100 supporting processes & threads | partially (we did disable dashboard) |
| **Polars** async executor (used by rllm dataset loading) | 1 thread per core ≈ **192** by default | ✅ `POLARS_MAX_THREADS` (we capped to 4) |
| **OpenMP / MKL / BLAS** inside torch | 1 thread per core ≈ **192** each, multiplied per worker | ✅ `OMP_NUM_THREADS` (we capped to 2) |
| **vLLM** workers (1 per GPU) + their own thread pools | ~50 each × 4 GPUs = ~200 | partially |
| **FSDP** distributed workers (4 GPUs × multiple processes) | ~10 per GPU | partially |

Even after capping every knob we control (polars, OMP, MKL, rayon, openblas, numexpr, tokenizers, vLLM multiproc method, ray cpus...), the Ray **`raylet`** alone tries to start 192 internal threads at boot. As soon as `pthread_create` hits the 1024 ceiling, it returns `EAGAIN`, `boost::asio` throws, the raylet receives SIGABRT, and the whole training process dies before vLLM ever loads the model.

This is what every failed run has shown:
1. First run: 24 000 lines of polars "Resource temporarily unavailable" panics (until we capped polars threads).
2. Second run: Ray dashboard `MetricsHead` subprocess EOF (we disabled the dashboard).
3. Third run: Ray's local raylet `boost::asio::detail::posix_thread::start_thread()` → SIGABRT — **same root cause**, just hit by a lower-level component.

## Why `taskset` / `numactl` don't fix it

I considered "fool the raylet into thinking there are only 32 CPUs". The raylet's C++ code reads `sysconf(_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN)`, which is the *system* CPU count, not the CPU *affinity* set by `taskset`. We tested it — even with `taskset -c 0-31`, Python still saw 192 cores. The only way to lie about online CPU count is via cgroups, which requires root.

## Why this isn't just a "tune things harder" problem

Every component we listed has a knob we can turn down — **except** the Ray raylet's internal `boost::asio` pool. That one is hardcoded to `hardware_concurrency()` in Ray ≥ 2.x. To run on this node we'd either need (a) a higher process limit, which only the cluster admin or a different node can provide, or (b) to rip Ray out of verl's trainer entirely (huge rewrite, GRPO group rollouts assume Ray actors).

## What "different node" means

The 1024-process ceiling is a **login-node policy**, not a cluster-wide thing. Compute nodes on Trillium typically allow 4096+ or unlimited per user. You don't have to write a batch script — `salloc --gpus-per-node=h100:4 --time=1:00:00` gives you an interactive shell on a real compute node where ray runs fine. That's still "SLURM" in the sense of the underlying scheduler, but it's not an `sbatch` queue — you sit in an interactive prompt the whole time.

If interactive `salloc` is also off the table (e.g., your account doesn't allow it, or you're getting nodes some other way), I need to know that mechanism so we can adapt. The smoke training **cannot** complete on a login node with `ulimit -u = 1024`.

Want me to (a) try `salloc` to grab an interactive GPU node, or (b) wait for you to provide whatever node you have access to and I'll mirror the setup there?

This is the same root cause I described in the prior turn (the raylet's internal `boost::asio` pool sized to `hardware_concurrency()` = 192 vs `ulimit -u 1024`). There's nothing left to tune from inside the container.

To proceed I need one of:
1. An interactive `salloc` GPU node (real compute node, higher ulimit),
2. The hostname/path of an alternate node you already hold, or
3. A clear no-go so I instead pivot to documenting the cluster-side fix request (admin raise `nproc` on the login node).
is ray needed for RL training? is it possible to do training without ray?

Short answer: **Ray is not required for RL training in general, but it *is* hard-required for THIS codebase** (rllm + verl).

## Why this codebase needs Ray

verl is architected around Ray actors:
- `AsyncActorRolloutRefWorker`, `CriticWorker`, `ActorRolloutRefWorker` are all `@ray.remote` classes.
- `RayWorkerGroup` orchestrates them.
- The `AgentPPOTrainer` does `ray.get(train_agent.remote(...))`, `ray.remote(max_concurrency=2048)(...)`, etc.
- async vLLM rollout (which the SWE training also uses) talks to Ray's actor pool.

Ripping Ray out is multi-day surgery. Not a workaround we can do tonight.

## Other RL frameworks that don't use Ray

If your goal is just *"prove I can run GRPO with metrics logged"*, these exist:

| Framework | Uses Ray? | GRPO support | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **TRL** (Hugging Face) | No (Accelerate) | ✅ `GRPOTrainer` | Simplest, runs on this login node with our current ulimit |
| **DeepSpeed-Chat** | No | RLHF/PPO | Needs DeepSpeed only |
| **trlx** | No | PPO | |
| **OpenRLHF (non-Ray mode)** | Optional | ✅ | Also installable, similar quality |

These would each let us train Qwen3-4B on a small RL task and produce per-step metric logs **today**, on this login node, with no Ray.

But — they're **not** what the paper / this repo uses. Metrics from TRL won't match what the SWE-Master paper reports. For the actual project, you'd still need verl/Ray eventually on a compute node.

## One Ray workaround worth a shot before giving up

`ray.init(local_mode=True)` runs all Ray actors **synchronously in the driver process** — no `raylet`, no GCS server, no plasma store. Process count stays tiny. The trade-off:
- Multi-GPU FSDP breaks (everything runs on one device)
- Async vLLM may not initialize correctly
- It's officially a debugging mode

For the FrozenLake smoke with Qwen3-4B (8 GB params on a single 80 GB H100), single-GPU is fine. It's a long shot — verl makes assumptions about real Ray actors — but it's the only Ray-side knob left that bypasses raylet thread spawning.

from typing import Any

import ray

from rllm.data import Dataset
from rllm.trainer.verl.train_agent_ppo import train_agent


class AgentTrainer:
    """
    A wrapper class that allows users to easily train custom agents with custom environments
    without having to directly interact with the underlying training infrastructure.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        agent_class: type,
        env_class: type,
        agent_args: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
        env_args: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
        config: dict[str, Any] | list[str] | None = None,
        train_dataset: Dataset | None = None,
        val_dataset: Dataset | None = None,
    ):
        """
        Initialize the AgentTrainer.

        Args:
            agent_class: The custom agent class to use for training
            env_class: The custom environment class to use for training
            config: Configuration overrides to apply to the default config
                   Can be a dictionary with dot notation keys (e.g., {"data.train_batch_size": 8})
                   or a list of strings in the format "key=value" (e.g., ["data.train_batch_size=8"])
            train_dataset: Optional train dataset to use
            val_dataset: Optional validation dataset to use
            agent_args: Optional arguments to pass to the agent class
            env_args: Optional arguments to pass to the environment class
        """
        self.agent_class = agent_class
        self.env_class = env_class
        self.agent_args = agent_args or {}
        self.env_args = env_args or {}

        self.config = config

        if train_dataset is not None and self.config is not None and hasattr(self.config, "data"):
            self.config.data.train_files = train_dataset.get_verl_data_path()
        if val_dataset is not None and self.config is not None and hasattr(self.config, "data"):
            self.config.data.val_files = val_dataset.get_verl_data_path()

    def train(self):
        if not ray.is_initialized():
            # include_dashboard=False — the dashboard's MetricsHead subprocess
            # fails to start on hosts with tight process limits (login-node
            # ulimit -u 1024), aborting node startup. We don't need it.
            ray.init(
                include_dashboard=False,
                runtime_env={
                    "env_vars": {"TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM": "true", "NCCL_DEBUG": "WARN"},
                    "pip": ["sentence_transformers"],
                },
            )

        ray.get(train_agent.remote(self.config, self.agent_class, self.env_class, self.agent_args, self.env_args))

class AgentTrainer:
    """
    A wrapper class that allows users to easily train custom agents with custom environments
    without having to directly interact with the underlying training infrastructure.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        agent_class: type,
        env_class: type,
        agent_args: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
        env_args: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
        config: dict[str, Any] | list[str] | None = None,
        train_dataset: Dataset | None = None,
        val_dataset: Dataset | None = None,
    ):
        """
        Initialize the AgentTrainer.

        Args:
            agent_class: The custom agent class to use for training
            env_class: The custom environment class to use for training
            config: Configuration overrides to apply to the default config
                   Can be a dictionary with dot notation keys (e.g., {"data.train_batch_size": 8})
                   or a list of strings in the format "key=value" (e.g., ["data.train_batch_size=8"])
            train_dataset: Optional train dataset to use
            val_dataset: Optional validation dataset to use
            agent_args: Optional arguments to pass to the agent class
            env_args: Optional arguments to pass to the environment class
        """
        self.agent_class = agent_class
        self.env_class = env_class
        self.agent_args = agent_args or {}
        self.env_args = env_args or {}

        self.config = config

        if train_dataset is not None and self.config is not None and hasattr(self.config, "data"):
            self.config.data.train_files = train_dataset.get_verl_data_path()
        if val_dataset is not None and self.config is not None and hasattr(self.config, "data"):
            self.config.data.val_files = val_dataset.get_verl_data_path()

    def train(self):
        if not ray.is_initialized():
            # local_mode runs every @ray.remote synchronously in the driver
            # process — no raylet, no GCS, no plasma store. Required on hosts
            # with tight nproc limits (login-node ulimit -u=1024 vs raylet's
            # 192-thread boost::asio pool). Set RLLM_RAY_LOCAL_MODE=0 to
            # disable on real compute nodes.
            ray.init(
                local_mode=os.environ.get("RLLM_RAY_LOCAL_MODE", "1") == "1",
                include_dashboard=False,
                runtime_env={
                    "env_vars": {"TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM": "true", "NCCL_DEBUG": "WARN"},
                    "pip": ["sentence_transformers"],
                },
            )

        ray.get(train_agent.remote(self.config, self.agent_class, self.env_class, self.agent_args, self.env_args))

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Smoke-test RL training: GRPO on FrozenLake with Qwen3-4B on a single node
# (4x H100 80GB on Trillium). Logs to console + tensorboard.
# Run inside the container — usually invoked by 04_train_frozenlake.sbatch.
set -euo pipefail

source "${VENV_BIN:-/scratch/$USER/swemaster/venv/rllm/bin}/activate"
cd "${PROJECT_ROOT:-/project/def-hemmati-ac/$USER/SWE-Master}/DeepSWE_RL/rllm"

export VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND=FLASH_ATTN
export PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF="expandable_segments:False"
export VLLM_USE_V1=1
export VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1
export VLLM_ENGINE_ITERATION_TIMEOUT_S=100000000000
export HYDRA_FULL_ERROR=1
export RAY_DEDUP_LOGS=0
export WANDB_MODE=offline

# Login-node has ulimit -u 1024 — polars/rayon/openmp will busts that without
# explicit caps. Each cap below maps to a different thread pool.
export POLARS_MAX_THREADS=${POLARS_MAX_THREADS:-4}
export RAYON_NUM_THREADS=${RAYON_NUM_THREADS:-4}
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=${OMP_NUM_THREADS:-2}
export MKL_NUM_THREADS=${MKL_NUM_THREADS:-2}
export NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS=${NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS:-2}
export OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=${OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS:-2}
export TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=${TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM:-false}
export RAY_num_cpus=${RAY_num_cpus:-32}
export VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=${VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD:-spawn}

# How many GPUs to use for training. Trillium nodes are 4x H100.
N_GPUS=${N_GPUS:-4}

# Run identifier for tensorboard + checkpoint dirs.
TS=$(date +"%Y-%m-%d_%H-%M-%S")

mkdir -p "${LOCAL_DIR}"

import os, glob

repo = os.environ.get("MODEL_ID","Qwen/Qwen3-4B").replace("/","--")
snapshots = glob.glob(os.path.join(hub, f"models--{repo}", "snapshots", "*"))
print(snapshots[0] if snapshots else os.environ["MODEL_ID"])
PY
)

content.text:
verl 0.7.1 hard-pins `ray[default]>=2.41.0`. Ray removed `local_mode` in 2.32+. So we can't downgrade ray without also downgrading verl, which means abandoning the rllm/verl integration this codebase is built on.

**Recap of the wall:**
- Login node `ulimit -u = 1024` (hard cap, no root).
- `raylet` boot allocates ~192 threads (one per CPU); plus 30 baseline procs leaves no room — SIGABRT.
- Ray `local_mode` (run-everything-in-driver) would skip raylet, but **was removed in Ray 2.32**, and verl pins `ray>=2.41`.
- Other Ray knobs don't expose raylet's internal `boost::asio` pool.

So at this point, the only way to make **this repo's RL pipeline** produce a metric line is to run it somewhere that allows more than 1024 threads. There's no internal config we haven't tried.

content.text:
Two more probes:
- Ray's `--num-cpus` is for resource scheduling, not the raylet's internal `boost::asio` pool — so no help.
- Apptainer's `--cpus` flag exists but **fails on this cluster**: the user-mode cgroup hierarchy lacks `cpu.max`. So we can't fence CPUs via Apptainer either.

One last technical option worth trying — an `LD_PRELOAD` shim that intercepts `sysconf(_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN)` and `get_nprocs()` to lie about CPU count. If raylet's `hardware_concurrency()` returns 8 instead of 192, its thread pool drops to 8 threads.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Smoke-test RL training: GRPO on FrozenLake with Qwen3-4B on a single node
# (4x H100 80GB on Trillium). Logs to console + tensorboard.
# Run inside the container — usually invoked by 04_train_frozenlake.sbatch.
set -euo pipefail

source "${VENV_BIN:-/scratch/$USER/swemaster/venv/rllm/bin}/activate"
cd "${PROJECT_ROOT:-/project/def-hemmati-ac/$USER/SWE-Master}/DeepSWE_RL/rllm"

export VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND=FLASH_ATTN
export PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF="expandable_segments:False"
export VLLM_USE_V1=1
export VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1
export VLLM_ENGINE_ITERATION_TIMEOUT_S=100000000000
export HYDRA_FULL_ERROR=1
export RAY_DEDUP_LOGS=0
export WANDB_MODE=offline

# Login-node has ulimit -u 1024 — polars/rayon/openmp will busts that without
# explicit caps. Each cap below maps to a different thread pool.
export POLARS_MAX_THREADS=${POLARS_MAX_THREADS:-4}
export RAYON_NUM_THREADS=${RAYON_NUM_THREADS:-4}
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=${OMP_NUM_THREADS:-2}
export MKL_NUM_THREADS=${MKL_NUM_THREADS:-2}
export NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS=${NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS:-2}
export OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=${OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS:-2}
export TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=${TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM:-false}
export RAY_num_cpus=${RAY_num_cpus:-32}

# are 4x H100 so for the real training (on a compute node where ulimit is OK)
# we'd flip RLLM_RAY_LOCAL_MODE=0 and bump N_GPUS=4.

export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=${CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES:-0}

# Run identifier for tensorboard + checkpoint dirs.
TS=$(date +"%Y-%m-%d_%H-%M-%S")

repo = os.environ.get("MODEL_ID","Qwen/Qwen3-4B").replace("/","--")
snapshots = glob.glob(os.path.join(hub, f"models--{repo}", "snapshots", "*"))
print(snapshots[0] if snapshots else os.environ["MODEL_ID"])

)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Wrap any command in the project's Apptainer container with all the right
# binds and cache redirections. Examples:
#   bash scripts/00_enter_container.sh bash scripts/01_build_env.sh
#   bash scripts/00_enter_container.sh python -c 'import torch; print(torch.cuda.is_available())'
#   bash scripts/00_enter_container.sh                # drop into shell
set -euo pipefail

USER=${USER:-$(whoami)}
SCRATCH=${SCRATCH:-/scratch/$USER}
PROJECT_ROOT=${PROJECT_ROOT:-/project/def-hemmati-ac/$USER/SWE-Master}
SIF=${SIF:-$SCRATCH/swemaster/sif/pytorch_27_cu128}     # sandbox dir OR .sif file
VENV=${VENV:-$SCRATCH/swemaster/venv/rllm}
HF_HOME_DIR=${HF_HOME_DIR:-$SCRATCH/swemaster/cache/hf}

if [[ ! -e "$SIF" ]]; then
  echo "[enter-container] container image not found at $SIF; build it first" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# Forbid cluster modules from leaking into the container.
module --force purge 2>/dev/null || true

mkdir -p "$HF_HOME_DIR" "$SCRATCH/swemaster/tmp"

# Container env vars: keep HF, pip, ray, torch caches on /scratch
export APPTAINERENV_HF_HOME="$HF_HOME_DIR"
export APPTAINERENV_HUGGINGFACE_HUB_CACHE="$HF_HOME_DIR/hub"
export APPTAINERENV_TRANSFORMERS_CACHE="$HF_HOME_DIR/transformers"
export APPTAINERENV_TORCH_HOME="$SCRATCH/swemaster/cache/torch"
export APPTAINERENV_PIP_CACHE_DIR="$SCRATCH/swemaster/cache/pip"
export APPTAINERENV_TMPDIR=/tmp
export APPTAINERENV_PROJECT_ROOT="$PROJECT_ROOT"
export APPTAINERENV_SCRATCH="$SCRATCH"
export APPTAINERENV_VENV="$VENV"
export APPTAINERENV_HF_HOME_DIR="$HF_HOME_DIR"

# Source the venv inside the container if it exists
APPTAINERENV_VENV_BIN=""
if [[ -d "$VENV/bin" ]]; then
  APPTAINERENV_VENV_BIN="$VENV/bin"
fi
export APPTAINERENV_VENV_BIN

# Build the command. Default is an interactive bash.
if [[ $# -eq 0 ]]; then
  CMD=(bash)
else
  CMD=("$@")
fi

# Binds: project (ro is too restrictive — many caches write into the repo);
# scratch for everything mutable.
exec apptainer exec --nv --cleanenv \
  --env "PATH=${VENV}/bin:/opt/conda/bin:/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin" \
  --env "USER=${USER}" \
  --env "HOME=${HOME}" \
  -B "$PROJECT_ROOT" \
  -B "$SCRATCH" \
  "$SIF" "${CMD[@]}"

content.text: what happened

## Where we ended up

**Done & ready (won't need to redo):**
- ✅ Apptainer sandbox built on `/scratch` (PyTorch 2.7 + CUDA 12.8, ~16 GB)
- ✅ Python venv inside it: rllm + verl 0.7.1 + vLLM 0.10.2 + flash-attn 2.8.3 + tensorboard + ray 2.55.1
- ✅ Qwen3-4B model downloaded (7.6 GB on `/scratch`)
- ✅ FrozenLake dataset registered (10 000 train / 100 test)
- ✅ All helper scripts written ([scripts/](scripts/))

**Smoke training: 4 attempts, all died before producing a single metric line:**

| # | Crash | Root cause | Fixed by |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `TypeError` on `os.path.join(None, …)` | unexported shell var | `export HF_HUB` |
| 2 | 24 000 polars panics — `EAGAIN` | thread storm | `POLARS_MAX_THREADS=4` + other caps |
| 3 | `MetricsHead failed to start` | Ray dashboard subprocess | `include_dashboard=False` |
| 4 | `SIGABRT` in `raylet` `boost::asio` thread pool | **`ulimit -u = 1024` vs ~192 raylet threads + workers + dashboard remnants** | **no fix from inside the container** |
| 5 | `RuntimeError: local_mode is no longer supported` | Ray removed local_mode in ≥ 2.32 | **can't downgrade — verl 0.7.1 pins `ray>=2.41`** |

## The bottom line

The login node policy is `ulimit -u 1024` (process+thread cap, no root). Ray's `raylet` alone tries to spawn ~192 threads on this 192-core box during init. We can't lower the raylet's thread pool (no public knob), can't bump the ulimit (no root), can't bypass Ray (verl is built around it), can't use Ray's old `local_mode` escape hatch (removed two versions before verl's minimum).

GPU availability doesn't help here — even 4 fully idle H100s can't paper over the process-count cap.

## Paths still open

1. **Interactive `salloc` GPU node** — compute nodes have ulimit ≥ 4096; ray works there. This is the only path that keeps verl/rllm.
2. **Pivot to TRL** (no Ray) — produces metric logs on this login node tonight, but uses a different RL framework than the paper.
3. **Wait** — pause until you have proper compute access; I resume from where we are.

You said GPUs are available but didn't say which node/mechanism — I need to know that before I can move forward, because the constraint is the policy on **this** machine, not the GPUs.

content.text:
The probe is conclusive — `taskset` is **not enough**:

```
std::thread::hardware_concurrency = 192   ← what raylet's boost::asio reads
sysconf(_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN)     = 192   ← unchanged by taskset
CPU_COUNT(sched_getaffinity)      = 8     ← affinity correctly set, but nobody asks
```

`taskset` correctly pins our process to 8 cores at the kernel level (`sched_getaffinity` = 8), but **the C++ library reads `sysconf(_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN)` which queries `/sys/devices/system/cpu/online` — system-wide, ignores affinity**. So raylet still thinks there are 192 cores and tries to launch 192 threads.

But — there's still a way to make raylet see "8 cores": **`LD_PRELOAD` a tiny shim** that intercepts `sysconf` and returns whatever we want. This is a standard HPC trick on shared boxes. Steps:

# TRL_RL — GRPO training on this cluster without Ray

This directory contains a self-contained TRL-based RL training pipeline. It
exists because the main `DeepSWE_RL/` stack (verl + Ray + vLLM async) cannot
boot on the Trillium **login node** — Ray's `raylet` allocates a thread pool
sized to `hardware_concurrency()` (192 here) and the user has `ulimit -u 1024`
(no root, hard cap). See `scripts/README.md` at the repo root for the full
diagnostic.

TRL uses 🤗 Accelerate (no Ray daemon), so process count stays under the
ulimit. The pipeline here is intentionally minimal — its job is to **produce
per-step RL metric logs** to verify the training infrastructure works on this
cluster, not to reproduce the SWE-Master paper.

When/if you get an interactive `salloc` GPU compute node, switch back to
`DeepSWE_RL/` for the faithful pipeline.

## Layout

```
TRL_RL/
├── README.md
├── configs/
│   └── smoke.yaml           # GRPO hyperparameters for the smoke run
├── src/
│   ├── train_grpo.py        # GRPOTrainer entry point
│   ├── rewards.py           # reward function(s) — synthetic + GSM8K
│   └── data.py              # dataset builders
└── scripts/
    ├── 00_install_trl.sh    # add trl into the existing apptainer venv
    └── 01_train_smoke.sh    # launch the smoke run inside the container
```

The Apptainer container, Python venv, and HF cache are **reused** from the
DeepSWE_RL setup at `/scratch/$USER/swemaster/{sif,venv,cache}/...` — we just
add the `trl` wheel on top.

## Run order

```bash
# 1. Install TRL on top of the existing venv (one-time)
bash scripts/00_enter_container.sh bash TRL_RL/scripts/00_install_trl.sh

# 2. Launch the smoke run (writes tensorboard + console logs)
bash scripts/00_enter_container.sh bash TRL_RL/scripts/01_train_smoke.sh
```

Outputs land at `/scratch/$USER/swemaster/runs/trl-smoke/<experiment>/`.

## Smoke task

A trivial *verifiable* task: the model is given a prompt asking it to emit a
specific token (e.g. `"YES"`), and the reward function returns `1.0` if that
token appears in the completion, else `0.0`. This is enough to drive GRPO
through real rollout → reward → advantage → policy update cycles and have
TRL emit per-step `train/reward`, `train/loss`, `train/kl`, etc. lines.

## What this is NOT

- Not a SWE-bench environment. SWE rollouts require Docker/Apptainer per
  instance, which is still TODO on this cluster.
- Not GRPO-on-Qwen-2.5-Coder-32B-SFT. Different base model, different reward.
- Not a faithful reproduction of the SWE-Master paper's metrics.

For the real pipeline, see `../DeepSWE_RL/` and run from a compute node.

"""Dataset builders for the TRL_RL smoke pipeline.

Datasets are returned as plain HuggingFace ``Dataset`` objects with a
``prompt`` column (and ``answer`` where applicable). TRL's GRPOTrainer
auto-tokenizes them.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import random
from datasets import Dataset


def yes_synthetic(n: int = 512, seed: int = 0) -> Dataset:
    """Trivial verifiable task: ask the model to emit ``YES``.

    Variety in the prompt wording keeps the model from memorizing a single
    token sequence — we still want a real distribution over rollouts.
    """
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    templates = [
        "Reply with the single word YES.",
        "Are you ready? Answer YES.",
        "If you understand, say YES.",
        "Please type YES.",
        "To confirm, output YES and nothing else.",
        "Just respond with: YES",
    ]
    prompts = [rng.choice(templates) for _ in range(n)]
    return Dataset.from_dict({"prompt": prompts})


def gsm8k_subset(n: int = 256, split: str = "train") -> Dataset:
    """GSM8K subset for a slightly less trivial smoke task.

    Only used when ``--dataset gsm8k`` is passed; not the default to keep the
    smoke fast and avoid an extra HF download.
    """
    from datasets import load_dataset
    raw = load_dataset("gsm8k", "main", split=split)
    raw = raw.shuffle(seed=0).select(range(min(n, len(raw))))

    def _to_prompt_answer(ex):
        # gold answer comes after the literal "#### " token in GSM8K
        gold = ex["answer"].split("####")[-1].strip()
        return {
            "prompt": ex["question"].strip() + "\nLet's reason step by step.",
            "answer": gold,
        }

    return raw.map(_to_prompt_answer, remove_columns=raw.column_names)

"""TRL GRPO smoke training.

Designed to run on the Trillium login node where ``ulimit -u = 1024`` makes
Ray-based trainers (verl / rllm) impossible. Uses HF Accelerate, no Ray,
no vLLM async — just enough machinery for GRPO to do rollout → reward →
advantage → loss → log.

Per-step metrics are emitted to stdout AND TensorBoard event files under
``--logging-dir``.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
from trl import GRPOConfig, GRPOTrainer

# Make sibling modules importable when this file is run as a script.
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
from data import yes_synthetic, gsm8k_subset  # noqa: E402
from rewards import yes_token_reward, gsm8k_numeric_match  # noqa: E402


def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    p.add_argument("--model-path", required=True,
                   help="Local HF snapshot dir, e.g. Qwen3-4B snapshot.")
    p.add_argument("--output-dir", required=True,
                   help="Where TRL writes checkpoints & state.")
    p.add_argument("--logging-dir", required=True,
                   help="TensorBoard event files go here.")
    p.add_argument("--dataset", choices=["yes", "gsm8k"], default="yes")
    p.add_argument("--max-steps", type=int, default=5)
    p.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, default=2,
                   help="Per-device train batch (prompts per step).")
    p.add_argument("--num-generations", type=int, default=4,
                   help="GRPO group size — completions sampled per prompt.")
    p.add_argument("--max-prompt-length", type=int, default=128)
    p.add_argument("--max-completion-length", type=int, default=64)
    p.add_argument("--learning-rate", type=float, default=1e-6)
    p.add_argument("--bf16", action="store_true", default=True)
    p.add_argument("--use-vllm", action="store_true",
                   help="Use vLLM for rollout. Off by default to keep "
                        "process count low on the login node.")
    return p.parse_args()


def main() -> None:
    args = parse_args()

    print(f"[trl-grpo] model={args.model_path}")
    print(f"[trl-grpo] dataset={args.dataset}  max_steps={args.max_steps}")
    print(f"[trl-grpo] output={args.output_dir}")
    print(f"[trl-grpo] tensorboard={args.logging_dir}")

    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(args.model_path, trust_remote_code=True)
    if tokenizer.pad_token_id is None:
        tokenizer.pad_token = tokenizer.eos_token

    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
        args.model_path,
        torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16 if args.bf16 else torch.float32,
        trust_remote_code=True,
    )

    if args.dataset == "yes":
        train_dataset = yes_synthetic(n=max(64, args.batch_size * args.max_steps * 4))
        reward_funcs = yes_token_reward
    else:
        train_dataset = gsm8k_subset(n=max(64, args.batch_size * args.max_steps * 4))
        reward_funcs = gsm8k_numeric_match

    config = GRPOConfig(
        output_dir=args.output_dir,
        logging_dir=args.logging_dir,
        per_device_train_batch_size=args.batch_size,
        gradient_accumulation_steps=1,
        num_generations=args.num_generations,
        max_prompt_length=args.max_prompt_length,
        max_completion_length=args.max_completion_length,
        learning_rate=args.learning_rate,
        max_steps=args.max_steps,
        logging_steps=1,
        save_steps=max(args.max_steps, 1) * 100,  # don't checkpoint during smoke
        save_total_limit=1,
        bf16=args.bf16,
        report_to=["tensorboard"],
        use_vllm=args.use_vllm,
        # Keep dataloader workers low to avoid thread/process pressure.
        dataloader_num_workers=0,
        # GRPO defaults a high beta; smoke is fine with the default.
        seed=0,
    )

    trainer = GRPOTrainer(
        model=model,
        reward_funcs=reward_funcs,
        args=config,
        train_dataset=train_dataset,
        processing_class=tokenizer,
    )

    print("[trl-grpo] starting trainer.train() ...")
    trainer.train()
    print("[trl-grpo] DONE")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

                   help="Use vLLM for rollout. Off by default to keep "
                        "process count low on the login node.")
    return p.parse_args()


def main() -> None:
    args = parse_args()

    print(f"[trl-grpo] model={args.model_path}")
    print(f"[trl-grpo] dataset={args.dataset}  max_steps={args.max_steps}")
    print(f"[trl-grpo] output={args.output_dir}")
    print(f"[trl-grpo] tensorboard={args.logging_dir}")

    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(args.model_path, trust_remote_code=True)
    if tokenizer.pad_token_id is None:
        tokenizer.pad_token = tokenizer.eos_token

    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
        args.model_path,
        torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16 if args.bf16 else torch.float32,
        trust_remote_code=True,
    )

    if args.dataset == "yes":
        train_dataset = yes_synthetic(n=max(64, args.batch_size * args.max_steps * 4))
        reward_funcs = yes_token_reward
    else:
        train_dataset = gsm8k_subset(n=max(64, args.batch_size * args.max_steps * 4))
        reward_funcs = gsm8k_numeric_match

    config = GRPOConfig(
        output_dir=args.output_dir,
        logging_dir=args.logging_dir,
        per_device_train_batch_size=args.batch_size,
        gradient_accumulation_steps=1,
        num_generations=args.num_generations,
        max_prompt_length=args.max_prompt_length,
        max_completion_length=args.max_completion_length,
        learning_rate=args.learning_rate,
        max_steps=args.max_steps,
        logging_steps=1,
        save_steps=max(args.max_steps, 1) * 100,  # don't checkpoint during smoke
        save_total_limit=1,
        bf16=args.bf16,
        report_to=["tensorboard"],
        use_vllm=args.use_vllm,
        # Keep dataloader workers low to avoid thread/process pressure.
        dataloader_num_workers=0,
        # GRPO defaults a high beta; smoke is fine with the default.
        seed=0,
    )

    trainer = GRPOTrainer(
        model=model,
        reward_funcs=reward_funcs,
        args=config,
        train_dataset=train_dataset,
        processing_class=tokenizer,
    )

    print("[trl-grpo] starting trainer.train() ...")
    trainer.train()
    print("[trl-grpo] DONE")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""TRL GRPO smoke training.

Designed to run on the Trillium login node where ``ulimit -u = 1024`` makes
Ray-based trainers (verl / rllm) impossible. Uses HF Accelerate, no Ray,
no vLLM async — just enough machinery for GRPO to do rollout → reward →
advantage → loss → log.

Per-step metrics are emitted to stdout AND TensorBoard event files under
``--logging-dir``.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
from trl import GRPOConfig, GRPOTrainer

# Make sibling modules importable when this file is run as a script.
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
from data import yes_synthetic, gsm8k_subset  # noqa: E402
from rewards import yes_token_reward, gsm8k_numeric_match  # noqa: E402


def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    p.add_argument("--model-path", required=True,
                   help="Local HF snapshot dir, e.g. Qwen3-4B snapshot.")
    p.add_argument("--output-dir", required=True,
                   help="Where TRL writes checkpoints & state.")
    p.add_argument("--logging-dir", required=True,
                   help="TensorBoard event files go here.")
    p.add_argument("--dataset", choices=["yes", "gsm8k"], default="yes")
    p.add_argument("--max-steps", type=int, default=5)
    p.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, default=2,
                   help="Per-device train batch (prompts per step).")
    p.add_argument("--num-generations", type=int, default=4,
                   help="GRPO group size — completions sampled per prompt.")
    p.add_argument("--max-prompt-length", type=int, default=128)
    p.add_argument("--max-completion-length", type=int, default=64)
    p.add_argument("--learning-rate", type=float, default=1e-6)
    p.add_argument("--bf16", action="store_true", default=True)
    p.add_argument("--use-vllm", action="store_true",
                   help="Use vLLM for rollout. Off by default to keep "
                        "process count low on the login node.")
    return p.parse_args()


def main() -> None:
    args = parse_args()

    print(f"[trl-grpo] model={args.model_path}")
    print(f"[trl-grpo] dataset={args.dataset}  max_steps={args.max_steps}")
    print(f"[trl-grpo] output={args.output_dir}")
    print(f"[trl-grpo] tensorboard={args.logging_dir}")

    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(args.model_path, trust_remote_code=True)
    if tokenizer.pad_token_id is None:
        tokenizer.pad_token = tokenizer.eos_token

    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
        args.model_path,
        torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16 if args.bf16 else torch.float32,
        trust_remote_code=True,
    )

    if args.dataset == "yes":
        train_dataset = yes_synthetic(n=max(64, args.batch_size * args.max_steps * 4))
        reward_funcs = yes_token_reward
    else:
        train_dataset = gsm8k_subset(n=max(64, args.batch_size * args.max_steps * 4))
        reward_funcs = gsm8k_numeric_match

    config = GRPOConfig(
        output_dir=args.output_dir,
        logging_dir=args.logging_dir,
        per_device_train_batch_size=args.batch_size,
        gradient_accumulation_steps=1,
        num_generations=args.num_generations,
        max_prompt_length=args.max_prompt_length,
        max_completion_length=args.max_completion_length,
        learning_rate=args.learning_rate,
        max_steps=args.max_steps,
        logging_steps=1,
        save_steps=max(args.max_steps, 1) * 100,  # don't checkpoint during smoke
        save_total_limit=1,
        bf16=args.bf16,
        report_to=["tensorboard"],
        use_vllm=args.use_vllm,
        # Keep dataloader workers low to avoid thread/process pressure.
        dataloader_num_workers=0,
        # GRPO defaults a high beta; smoke is fine with the default.
        seed=0,
    )

    trainer = GRPOTrainer(
        model=model,
        reward_funcs=reward_funcs,
        args=config,
        train_dataset=train_dataset,
        processing_class=tokenizer,
    )

    print("[trl-grpo] starting trainer.train() ...")
    trainer.train()
    print("[trl-grpo] DONE")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    p.add_argument("--dataset", choices=["yes", "gsm8k"], default="yes")
    p.add_argument("--max-steps", type=int, default=5)
    p.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, default=2,
                   help="Per-device train batch (prompts per step).")
    p.add_argument("--num-generations", type=int, default=4,
                   help="GRPO group size — completions sampled per prompt.")
    # TRL 0.29 removed max_prompt_length — prompt truncation is handled by the
    # tokenizer's model_max_length. We pass --max-prompt-length so we can clamp
    # the tokenizer; the GRPOConfig only consumes max_completion_length.
    p.add_argument("--max-prompt-length", type=int, default=128)
    p.add_argument("--max-completion-length", type=int, default=64)
    p.add_argument("--learning-rate", type=float, default=1e-6)
    p.add_argument("--bf16", action="store_true", default=True)
    p.add_argument("--use-vllm", action="store_true",
                   help="Use vLLM for rollout. Off by default to keep "
                        "process count low on the login node.")
    return p.parse_args()


def main() -> None:
    args = parse_args()

    print(f"[trl-grpo] model={args.model_path}")
    print(f"[trl-grpo] dataset={args.dataset}  max_steps={args.max_steps}")
    print(f"[trl-grpo] output={args.output_dir}")
    print(f"[trl-grpo] tensorboard={args.logging_dir}")

    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(args.model_path, trust_remote_code=True)
    if tokenizer.pad_token_id is None:
        tokenizer.pad_token = tokenizer.eos_token
    tokenizer.model_max_length = args.max_prompt_length

    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
        args.model_path,
        torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16 if args.bf16 else torch.float32,
        trust_remote_code=True,
    )

    if args.dataset == "yes":
        train_dataset = yes_synthetic(n=max(64, args.batch_size * args.max_steps * 4))
        reward_funcs = yes_token_reward
    else:
        train_dataset = gsm8k_subset(n=max(64, args.batch_size * args.max_steps * 4))
        reward_funcs = gsm8k_numeric_match

    config = GRPOConfig(
        output_dir=args.output_dir,
        logging_dir=args.logging_dir,
        per_device_train_batch_size=args.batch_size,
        gradient_accumulation_steps=1,
        num_generations=args.num_generations,
        max_prompt_length=args.max_prompt_length,
        max_completion_length=args.max_completion_length,
        learning_rate=args.learning_rate,
        max_steps=args.max_steps,
        logging_steps=1,
        save_steps=max(args.max_steps, 1) * 100,  # don't checkpoint during smoke
        save_total_limit=1,
        bf16=args.bf16,
        report_to=["tensorboard"],
        use_vllm=args.use_vllm,
        # Keep dataloader workers low to avoid thread/process pressure.
        dataloader_num_workers=0,
        # GRPO defaults a high beta; smoke is fine with the default.
        seed=0,
    )

    trainer = GRPOTrainer(
        model=model,
        reward_funcs=reward_funcs,
        args=config,
        train_dataset=train_dataset,
        processing_class=tokenizer,
    )

    print("[trl-grpo] starting trainer.train() ...")
    trainer.train()
    print("[trl-grpo] DONE")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

The "original" data is here locally — 3-row demo of the paper's RL dataset format at [data_examples/rl_data/ood_data/.../train_00000.parquet](data_examples/rl_data/ood_data/equal_0.3999999_0.9999999_swe-gym_and_rebench_demo_for_RL/train_00000.parquet). Each row has `problem_statement` (the issue text), `patch` (gold fix), `test_patch`, `docker_image`, etc.

**Key constraint**: the *proper* reward is "apply model patch, run tests in the docker image, count passes". That needs the Apptainer SWE-bench backend we haven't built yet. For training on this dataset *today*, we use a **proxy reward**: text-similarity between the model's diff and the gold `patch`. Honest about the trade-off — it gives us a real gradient signal on real SWE data, just not the paper's test-based reward.

Adding this to the existing TRL_RL pipeline.

    Each row is a real SWE-bench task. Columns we use:

    Other columns (``test_patch``, ``docker_image``, ``FAIL_TO_PASS``, ...)

            problem_statement=row["problem_statement"],

"""Dataset builders for the TRL_RL smoke pipeline.

Datasets are returned as plain HuggingFace ``Dataset`` objects with a
``prompt`` column (and ``answer`` where applicable). TRL's GRPOTrainer
auto-tokenizes them.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import random
from datasets import Dataset


def yes_synthetic(n: int = 512, seed: int = 0) -> Dataset:
    """Trivial verifiable task: ask the model to emit ``YES``.

    Variety in the prompt wording keeps the model from memorizing a single
    token sequence — we still want a real distribution over rollouts.
    """
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    templates = [
        "Reply with the single word YES.",
        "Are you ready? Answer YES.",
        "If you understand, say YES.",
        "Please type YES.",
        "To confirm, output YES and nothing else.",
        "Just respond with: YES",
    ]
    prompts = [rng.choice(templates) for _ in range(n)]
    return Dataset.from_dict({"prompt": prompts})


def gsm8k_subset(n: int = 256, split: str = "train") -> Dataset:
    """GSM8K subset for a slightly less trivial smoke task.

    Only used when ``--dataset gsm8k`` is passed; not the default to keep the
    smoke fast and avoid an extra HF download.
    """
    from datasets import load_dataset
    raw = load_dataset("gsm8k", "main", split=split)
    raw = raw.shuffle(seed=0).select(range(min(n, len(raw))))

    def _to_prompt_answer(ex):
        # gold answer comes after the literal "#### " token in GSM8K
        gold = ex["answer"].split("####")[-1].strip()
        return {
            "prompt": ex["question"].strip() + "\nLet's reason step by step.",
            "answer": gold,
        }

    return raw.map(_to_prompt_answer, remove_columns=raw.column_names)
